name: Venice
tagline: Private, unfiltered AI chat and image generation running on open-weight models, with history kept in your browser instead of on a server.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The product is a chat UI plus image generation in front of open-weight models, and the chat UI part is a solved one-shot build. An agent can give you streaming chat, a model picker, an editable system prompt, and local-only history in a single sitting, and if you point it at Ollama on your own machine the privacy story is actually stronger than Venice's, because nothing leaves the box. What you cannot conjure is the inference: the models people actually want Venice for are large, and running them well means either a serious GPU or a third-party API, which reintroduces exactly the trust problem you were paying to avoid. Image generation locally is its own install-and-tune project, not a line in a prompt. So: yes for the interface, no for the thing underneath it.
coreLoopDIY: A local web chat client that streams from Ollama or an API-key provider, lets you edit the system prompt per conversation, and stores every thread in browser storage only.
requirements: Ollama installed locally, or an API key for an open-weight model host
Enough RAM/VRAM for whatever model you pick, which is the real constraint
Node 20+ to run the dev server
A separate local Stable Diffusion setup if you want images
whatYouLose: Access to large models you cannot fit on consumer hardware
Built-in image generation that works on the first click
A phone-friendly hosted app you can open anywhere without a tunnel
Whatever uptime and throughput their GPU supply buys you
Someone else's word that your prompts are not logged, replaced by the burden of checking your own provider
moatNotes: The moat is GPUs and the credibility of a privacy claim, not code. Neither is something an agent writes.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the hard part is not the chat box, it is having a large uncensored model answer in two seconds from a phone on a train. Venice sells inference capacity and a stated no-logs posture at a flat monthly rate, which is cheaper and far less annoying than buying a GPU, and more trustworthy to most people than reading the terms of service of some API reseller. If you already own hardware that can run a 70B model, the subscription is mostly redundant. If you do not, the subscription is the entire product.
notes: The UI is a weekend's worth of fun and a day's worth of work; the GPU bill is the subscription.
prompt:
Build a local-only private AI chat client in an empty folder. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript on the front end, a tiny Node 20 Express server for proxying model calls so API keys never reach the browser. Plain CSS, no component library. pnpm.

Core behavior:
- Chat view with streaming token-by-token responses rendered as markdown, with code blocks syntax highlighted.
- Model picker populated at runtime: query the local Ollama API at http://localhost:11434/api/tags for installed models, and if OPENROUTER_API_KEY is present in .env also list a hardcoded short array of open-weight models from that provider. Clearly label which models are local and which leave the machine.
- Per-conversation system prompt, editable in a side panel, saved with the thread. Ship three presets: blunt assistant, coding assistant, no refusals beyond what the model itself enforces.
- Temperature and max tokens sliders, persisted.
- Multi-conversation sidebar: new, rename, delete, search by title and body.

Storage: all threads in IndexedDB via idb-keyval, nothing server-side. Add an Export all JSON button and an Import that merges. Add a Delete everything button with one confirm step.

Server: a single POST /chat endpoint that streams from either Ollama or OpenRouter depending on the selected model, and nothing else. Secrets only from .env via dotenv, with a committed .env.example. Never log prompt or response bodies.

Out of scope, do not build: image generation, user auth, hosting, mobile app, voice, file uploads, RAG, any database server.

Deliverables: working pnpm dev with both server and client, and a README that states plainly which model choices keep data on the machine and which do not.
